newsitem.title: JAPAN: No plan to change Japan economic assessment -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: No plan to change Japan economic assessment -- EPA.

text.p: Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) does not plan to alter its assessment of the economy in its upcoming monthly report, EPA Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told said on Friday.

"We're not in a situation to either strengthen or weaken the economic assessment in the next monthly economic report," Nukaya said, adding that the effects of the rise in the national consumption tax was within expectatons.
Japan raised its consumption tax to five percent from three on April 1.
Nukaya also said that production was moving within an expected range and was still in a rising trend.

April industrial production data released on Thursday showed a preliminary drop of 0.4 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis. Expectations has been for a flat figure or a slight rise.

"We had expected a slowdown (in production) in the April-June period. Since the rise up until the January-March period was rather high, it can be said that production is, within expectations, on a rising trend," Nukaya said.
